newsitem.title: INDIA: Kazakh leader says C.Asia wary of fundamentalism.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh leader says C.Asia wary of fundamentalism.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev said on Monday that the Central Asian republics were opposed to the spread of Moslem fundamentalism in the region.
"None of the Central Asian states wants fundamentalism to permeate their societies," Nazarbayev, commenting on strife in Afghanistan, told reporters at the start of a three-day visit to India.

Nazarbayev was given a colourful reception at Delhi's British-built presidential palace. He was due to hold talks with President Shankar Dayal Sharma and Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda later on Monday.
Asked to comment on the Afghan conflict, Nazarbayev said: "The Central Asian countries for years have been brought up on a notion of atheism."
He said developments in Afghanistan had been closely reviewed by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), including Russia.
He said the CIS had made its own evaluation of the situation in Afghanistan, including the stance of the Islamic Taleban movement that seized the Afghan capital Kabul in late September.
"However, these events are happening in the neighbouring countries. We believe those are internal affairs of those countries," he said without elaborating.
Nazarbayev was asked if Kazakhstan shared India's view that the Taleban were a fundamentalist Moslem group.
"I cannot take a position. However, I am free to do that judging by the actions that they are taking," he said.
Nazarbayev said Afghanistan was not on the agenda for his talks with Indian leaders. But Indian officials said his hosts would raise the issue with him.
Indian and Kazakh officials were expected to sign investment and tax agreements later on Monday.
